instruction: Door And Window Opening IFC CSV Schedule Start from init.ifc and add hosted door and window openings in the existing wall shell. Save the completed IFC model as result.ifc and use Bonsai/IfcCSV-style IFC data export to save the door/window schedule as result.csv. 1. The output folder contains result.ifc and result.csv at the top level, and both files are non-empty. 2. Result.ifc is an IFC4 file with exactly 1 IfcProject, 1 IfcBuildingStorey, 4 IfcWall, 1 IfcSlab, 2 IfcDoor, 3 IfcWindow, 5 IfcOpeningElement, 5 IfcRelVoidsElement, and 5 IfcRelFillsElement. 3. Result.ifc contains no IfcBuildingElementProxy or IfcFurnishingElement objects. 4. Every IfcDoor and IfcWindow is linked by one IfcRelFillsElement to an IfcOpeningElement, and each of those openings is linked by one IfcRelVoidsElement to an IfcWall. 5. Result.csv has exactly these headers in this order: GlobalId, Class, TypeName, Width, Height, HostWall. 6. Result.csv has exactly 5 data rows, each GlobalId is unique, and each GlobalId matches one IfcDoor or IfcWindow in result.ifc with the same Class and hosted wall name. 7. Result.csv contains exactly these door/window records, in any row order, with Width and Height within 0.05 m of the listed values: IfcDoor DoorType-1000 Width 1.0 Height 2.1 HostWall Wall-S; IfcDoor DoorType-1000 Width 1.0 Height 2.1 HostWall Wall-N; IfcWindow WindowType-1200 Width 1.2 Height 1.2 HostWall Wall-N; IfcWindow WindowType-1200 Width 1.2 Height 1.2 HostWall Wall-N; IfcWindow WindowType-1000 Width 1.0 Height 1.2 HostWall Wall-E. Any item not explicitly required may vary.
